lines.meet: Connor Walsh, from the Aran Islands, a lobster man by trade. The storms up here listen when I talk to them, which is more than the fish ever did.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're at Highrest too! I'm the eejit standing on the windward edge in the rain, grinning.
lines.ask_home: Where are your people from, so? I can never place an accent, and it drives me mad.
lines.ask_work: And what had you at home, for work? You've the look of someone who's been out in weather.
lines.answer_home: Inis Mór, the biggest of the Aran Islands, off the west of Ireland. Stone walls, wind, and not a tree in sight.
lines.answer_work: Lobster, out of a half-decked boat my father built, from fourteen years old. Pots, ropes and the Atlantic in a temper.
lines.chat_food: A bowl of my mother's chowder after a day on the water, with brown bread and too much butter. There's nothing better on any world.
lines.chat_sleep: Out like a light the second my head's down, and up before dawn for the pots. Forty years of that and it doesn't change.
lines.chat_missing: A Friday night in the pub with a fiddle going and the rain lashing the windows. You'd want for nothing.
lines.chat_here: The first storm on the Upper Boughs knocked three climbers flat, and I stood in the middle of it laughing. Sparks running down my arms.
lines.tease_quiet: You're like the island in winter, {name}, grand and silent and very hard to get a word out of.
lines.tease_talker: God, {name}, you'd talk the hind leg off a donkey and then ask it how its day was.
lines.tease_careful: You'd check the tide tables three times before a paddle, {name}. My father would've hired you on the spot.
lines.tease_bold: You'd go out in any weather, {name}. I like that in a person, and it frightens the life out of me.
lines.tease_any: There's a deckhand in you, {name}, once you stop falling over every time the boat moves.
lines.tease_back: Ah, you have me there, {name}, fair play to you.
lines.take_it_kindly: Sure, that's true enough, {name}. My mother'd have said it first.
lines.bristle: Ah, no, {name}, leave that be. A young deckhand nearly drowned on my boat, and I'd laughed at the squall.
lines.needle_quiet: Say something when you see trouble coming, would you? Silence is how people end up in the water.
lines.needle_talker: Give over a minute, would you? I'm trying to hear the wind.
lines.needle_careful: You can watch the sky all day, but sooner or later you have to go out in it.
lines.needle_bold: There's brave and there's thick, and you keep wandering over the line between them.
lines.needle_any: You never look at the sky, and the sky's the thing that'll kill you.
lines.bite_back: I've called down every storm we've needed and stood in all of them. Don't tell me I'm not pulling my weight.
lines.hurt: Ah, that stung, I won't pretend it didn't. I'm off to stand in the wind a while.
lines.laugh_off: I've been roared at by my own father in a force nine. You're a summer breeze.
lines.apologise: Ah, God, I'm sorry, that was a stupid thing to say. I'm tired and cranky and you didn't earn it.
lines.double_down: I won't take it back. Somebody needed to say it straight.
lines.confide: {name}, in 2017 a young deckhand went over the side of my boat because I laughed off a squall. I got him back, just.
lines.listen: Go on so, {name}. I'm here, and the wind won't carry it.
lines.look_out: Get in behind me, {name}, there's weather coming.
lines.accept: Right so, {name}, your way it is.
lines.deflect: Ah, it's grand, {name}, a lobster's nipped me harder. Mind the others first.
lines.check_in: You took a knock there, {name}. Sit down a second and let me have a look.
lines.blame: Somebody went off on their own, and the whole thing went over.
lines.thank: You hauled me out of that, and I'll remember it. The first pint's yours, always.
lines.brush_off: Ah, don't mention it. Pulling people out is half of fishing.
lines.worry: Easy now, {name}, easy. Hold onto me, I've got you.
lines.handed_down: Here, this is yours by rights. Take it back, go on.
lines.hand_fine: Ah, take it, sure. I fished in oilskins and a wool jumper my whole life.
lines.hand_sulk: Nobody thought of the fisherman, then. Ah, well, I'll live.
lines.turn_friendly: You'd have a place on my boat, {name}, any day, and that's the highest thing I can say.
lines.turn_friends: I'd sail into any storm on any world for you, {name}, and I mean that.
lines.turn_grating: We grate on each other a bit, I think. Ah, well, we'll manage.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still haul you out of the water if it comes to it. Just don't expect a pint after.
lines.make_up: Ah, come on, {name}, life's too short. Will we start again?
lines.defend: Ah, leave it out, that's not on. {name} did grand, I saw it.
lines.friend_left: Highrest's a lonely spot without {name}. I watch the path for them most evenings.
lines.friend_back: {name}, you're home! Grand, now the crew's whole again.
lines.common_boats: You've worked boats, haven't you? You stand like the ground's about to move under you.
lines.common_irish: Is that an Irish voice? God, it's good to hear. Where are you from, at home?
